title: Debug === vs == type coercion bugs in TypeScript — 3 turns
description: Multiple == coercion bugs causing wrong comparisons. Fix to ===, run tests, add TypeScript strict mode.

task_spec.prompt: The `isEqual` function in `src/utils.ts` uses `==` instead of `===`, causing type coercion bugs (e.g., `0 == ''` is true). Fix `isEqual` to use `===`. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
followup_prompts: Run `npm test -- --forceExit` to check the current state. Walk me through what you fixed. Now fix the remaining == bugs: in `isEmpty`, change `value == ''` to `value === ''` and `value == 0` to `value === 0` (keep `value == null` for the null/undefined check, which is idiomatic). Fix `parseId` to use `=== null || === undefined` instead of `== null`, and check `=== ''` instead of `== ''`. Fix `includesStrict` to use `===`. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
Final verification: run `npm test -- --forceExit` and confirm a completely clean build. Every test must pass — especially the edge case tests for parseId(0) and includesStrict with type mismatches.
success_criteria: isEmpty uses === for string and number checks
parseId treats numeric 0 as a valid ID
includesStrict uses === to prevent type coercion
